validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE / STATUS / FUEL / CAPACITY / LENGTH / FUELSOURCE / LOCATION. This is the El Paso Natural Gas (EPNG) system, one of the largest and best-documented interstate gas pipeline networks in the US -- founded 1928 by Paul Kayser, first deliveries 1929 (a 204-mile line from Jal, NM to El Paso, TX), extended to reach California in November 1947. It is unambiguously real, currently operating, and correctly classified as a large-diameter interstate gas transmission trunk (not a gathering/process line). Existence/current-operating-status is independently confirmed by a live 2022 Federal Register notice ('El Paso Natural Gas Company, L.L.C.; Notice of Initiation of Section 5 Proceeding') -- a FERC/government document, not KM- or GEM-derived -- plus ongoing trade-press coverage of a 2021 rupture/fire near Coolidge, AZ that took a segment of the live system out of service. GEM's exact figures (Capacity=5600 MMcf/d, LengthKnown=10140 mi, FuelSource='San Juan, Permian and Anadarko basins') are corroborated VERBATIM by two independent origins: (1) Kinder Morgan's own operator page ('El Paso Natural Gas (EPNG) is a 10,140-mile pipeline system... transports natural gas from the Rockies, San Juan, Permian and Anadarko basins... Capacity of 5,600 million cubic feet per day... 44 Bcf of underground working storage in Southeast New Mexico'), and (2) Rextag, an independent commercial pipeline-GIS/data provider, which states the identical '10140' miles and '5.6 Bcf/d' independently of Kinder Morgan's page. Wikipedia's article (now citable per 2026-08-27 policy) independently states the same 10,140-mile figure and the Permian(TX)/San Juan(NM,CO) origin -> West TX/NM/NV/CA/AZ destination description matching GEM's Location cluster (StartState=Texas, EndState=California) -- though Wikipedia's own footnote for the mile figure traces back toward the same operator material, so it is treated here as corroborating but not a fully independent third leg; Rextag is the genuinely separate second origin. Tier is HIGH on Status/Fuel/Capacity/Length/FuelSource/Location. DUPLICATE CHECK (against the 45-row TX-operating roster): P2577 is also named 'El Paso Gas Pipeline' (len=14.4 mi, dia=24in, cap=320 MMcf/d, updated same date 2023-08-16 as this row) -- checked and this is NOT a double-count. The gem.wiki page's own 'Expansion Projects' section documents P2577 as the 'Northern Delaware Basin Expansion Project,' a discrete EIA-tracked increment (14.4 mi / 23.2 km, 24-inch, 320 MMcf/d, completed February 2020) that added takeaway capacity from the Delaware Basin -- and I independently confirmed this project via EIA's own 'Today in Energy' article (eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=44856), which states verbatim: 'Completed in February 2020, this 14-mile, 0.32 Bcf/d expansion of the El Paso Natural Gas Transmission System (EPNG) increased takeaway capacity out of the Delaware Basin' -- an EIA-sourced, non-operator, non-GEM confirmation. P2577's 14.4 mi is 0.14% of P0184's 10,140-mi system total, i.e. exactly the network-vs-discrete-expansion-project granularity GEM uses elsewhere (parent trunk row + specific project rows), not a duplicate; no merge recommended. HARVESTED CITATION POOL: 12 citations harvested from this wiki page; I opened/checked 10 of 12 (bit.ly->Wikipedia redirect, both kindermorgan.com pages, the archived EPNG environmental-report PDF, eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php, the EIA todayinenergy article, the 2018 Pipeline & Gas Journal planned-projects PDF, and the naturalgasintel.com 2021-blast article). Two were access failures, not deletions: pstrust.org's incident map + its hosted NTSB PDF both 403 (bot-block), and the Wayback-archived FERC pipe-code list page timed out -- none of these bore on the core Length/Capacity/FuelSource/Owner values already double-corroborated above, so no gap remains open. See the separate StartYear1 finding (concern) and the separate Owner finding.

validity.researcher_notes: SPEC / DATE, unsupported. GEM records StartYear1=1997. I could not find any source -- operator, regulatory, or press -- that supports 1997 as an in-service, founding, or restructuring date for EPNG. Notably, gem.wiki's OWN infobox for this pipeline lists 'Start Year: 1997' with NO citation footnote attached (every other infobox field -- Owner[1], Capacity/Length[2], background[3], FERC code[4] -- carries a bracketed reference number; Start Year carries none), which is itself a signal the figure was never sourced even by the wiki editor. The well-documented history places EPNG's founding in 1928 (Paul Kayser; TSHA Handbook of Texas / company-history sources), first gas deliveries in 1929 (a 204-mile, 16-inch line from Jal, NM), and the extension that brought the mainline to California completed November 1947 (Wikipedia, company-history sources) -- none of which is 1997. I also checked for an unrelated corporate event that might explain '1997': the company began doing business as 'El Paso Energy Corporation' in 1996, and formally reorganized under a new holding-company structure on 1 August 1998 (SEC Form 8-K, 1998) -- 1997 falls in between but matches neither dated event, and in any case a holding-company rename/reorg is not a pipeline in-service date. This reads as either a data-entry artifact or possibly the earliest year covered by whatever dataset vintage first populated the field -- either way it is unsupported and should not be treated as reliable without further research.

validity.researcher_notes: ATTRIBUTION / OWNER. Kinder Morgan's own investor-relations announcement ('Kinder Morgan Energy Partners Increases Ownership Stake to 100 Percent in El Paso Natural Gas Pipeline and Midstream Assets,' dated 2013, describing the March 1, 2013 closing of KMP's purchase of the remaining 50% of El Paso Natural Gas Company, L.L.C. from Kinder Morgan, Inc.) is the direct, dated source for the exact 100% figure. Wikipedia independently corroborates that EPNG 'is owned by Kinder Morgan, Inc.' (the general ownership fact, not the specific 50%->100% transaction history), and no source found names any other owner at any point after 2013. I attempted to add a fully independent (non-KM) press source for the specific 2013 transaction -- Hart Energy covered it twice -- but both Hart Energy URLs returned HTTP 403 (bot-block) under url_verifier and could not be cited; this is an access failure, not evidence against the fact, which remains corroborated by KM's own dated corporate disclosure plus Wikipedia's independent general-ownership statement. Tier medium (one strong primary source for the precise 100% share, generally corroborated).

summary: Confirmed real, currently-operating, correctly-classified EPNG interstate trunk (10,140 mi / 5,600 MMcf/d / San Juan-Permian-Anadarko basins / Kinder Morgan 100%, all corroborated by Kinder Morgan + independent Rextag/Wikipedia/Federal Register sources); P2577 checked and confirmed NOT a duplicate (it is EPNG's separately EIA-tracked Northern Delaware Basin Expansion Project, 0.14% of this row's mileage). One UNRESOLVED concern: StartYear1=1997 is unsupported by any source, including gem.wiki's own uncited infobox entry -- flagged for Update, not pasted over.
